policy: Implement the complete game-developer usability audit in three phases. This board is authorized for implementation by the user and tracked by the active Codex goal. Projects are unlaunched and internally used: migrate owned callers, content and fixtures, then remove obsolete APIs/schema compatibility rather than accumulating shims. Do not remove useful current low-level/custom-composition APIs merely because examples now use a convenience API. Preserve unrelated work and historical raw evidence. For each failing check decide whether code or test contradicts the intended behavior; update stale assertions/fixtures with meaningful replacement coverage instead of preserving obsolete behavior or deleting valid guarantees. Follow odin_godot/AGENTS.md. Claim one task at a time with worker/token and record concrete changes and validation. Repository backlog: docs/design/usability-backlog.json. Board operations do not authorize parallel editing agents. Complete dependency work before architecture tasks; reassess designs when narrow fixes accumulate.

tasks.progress: Complete: Kit entities, inputs, callbacks, profiles, messages, codecs, events and backups resolve across module subpackages. Shipped HelloNet/HelloSim use entity packages with owner-side birth callbacks. Native peer journeys, schema/version relocation invariants and a real linked browser runtime pass.
review_notes: Independent read-only Kit review confirms a module-wide parse/resolve/emission design is necessary: root-only metadata, package-local input/entity IDs and game-aware callbacks cannot be fixed by deleting refusal checks.

Resolve code identity by normalized declaring package and symbol through each defining file import map. Import aliases and file location must not become wire identity. Existing explicit numeric entity IDs can anchor tagged-entity schemas, including same-named types in separate packages.

Input/profile/message wire roots require stable binding identities beyond numeric entity IDs; sort/deduplicate resolved input types by stable binding uses rather than textual import-qualified names. A deliberate ABI schema migration may replace the old frozen shipped-flat fingerprint assertion with relocation/alias invariance.

Keep one root boot/guard/import manifest and the real subpackage-to-root import-cycle prohibition. Move game-aware consequence/edge/tick/presentation adapters into the owning game package, using per-Session descriptor bindings rather than mutable package-global current-game callbacks.

Compare two callback designs before extending runtime: typed per-entity callback tables carried by bound command/sim descriptors versus owner-specific generated Command_Set/Sim_Set thunks through existing Entity_Kind bindings. Both must cover the generated local-authority command fast path and client prediction, not only received commands.

Acceptance needs moved HelloNet/HelloSim entities and inputs, actual peer gameplay, relocation/import-alias invariance, same-named type disambiguation and duplicate numeric-ID errors, two game instances with different callbacks, imported constraints/codecs/profiles/messages, local composed blocks, and native/Web generation. Replace obsolete root-only refusals with positive cases while retaining true import/alias isolation failures.

Selected the smaller design after second review: reuse existing Entity_Kind.set/sim_set and immutable owner-scoped Command_Set/Sim_Set/Edge_Desc thunks. The registry and tracked simulation already carry the binding; no new mutable global callback slots or runtime callback-context ABI fields are needed. Leaf-private implementation procedures may need narrow generated bridges.
test_diagnosis: The first generator regression invocation supplied SGEN_BIN but omitted Odin from PATH; a later compiler check correctly failed to launch odin. With the pinned compiler directory on PATH, the entire existing SCRIPTGEN_OK corpus passes. Baseline/new generator-only subpackage refusal and fingerprint checks both pass, and ten generated artifacts across three representative projects are byte-identical.

The new native test initially named a nonexistent Action_State enum; corrected its assertion to the actual outcome state. The WASM check initially included core:testing, whose OS/thread support is native-only; separated fixture gameplay helpers from the !freestanding test file so the actual generated adapters still compile for WASM.

A bare-import fixture exposed an existing generator bug: collect_file_imports bound a bare import to the target package clause. A minimal compiler experiment showed Odin binds the final path component. Corrected both generator lookup and the fixture spelling, deleted the redundant package-name filesystem scan, and verified alias/bare/flat contract invariance.

Adding the new check to the deliberately fixed twenty-check core selection was unnecessary and failed its metadata contract. Kept kitbindings as a separate registered check; the original core selection and all five selector tests pass unchanged.

A scripted edit stopped at an initializer-spacing assertion after saving main. Completed the dependent parse/generation edits before building or running consumers; the resulting generator compiles cleanly.
The initial resolved-input record used context as a field name, which Odin reserves. Renamed it ctx; no contract change.

Review found parse_sample still deduplicated raw parameter spellings before import resolution. Removed that obsolete early check and made resolved identity the authority; added positive different-file/same-spelling and negative same-declaration/different-alias coverage.

Review found redundant raw replicated/input type spelling in net_fingerprint changed on alias-only edits despite identical canonical ABI. Those entries now use their normalized ABI representation while the recursive canonical schema continues to distinguish real type/layout changes; targeted invariance and mutation tests pass.
Generic parameter kinds cannot be recovered from source spans alone: Odin parser Typeid_Type nodes have an empty span. Read the AST kind explicitly; real generic composition regressions then pass.

A remaining shallow fingerprint walk discarded generic bindings, and emitted tick thunks retained authored import aliases absent from generated files. Passed Type_Use through both walks and separated tick input code spelling/imports from semantic identity.

Review exposed nonwire generic caches/backups/signals being forced through a wire-only renderer. Added a bounded AST-based code-type renderer, kept wire admissibility separate, and left irrelevant untagged opaque containers to the compiler. Context-preserving composition now also handles the real Replay Session graph.

Ordinary aliases introduced an artificial ::<base> schema layer. Removed that layer for transparent aliases while retaining enum/distinct representation, so public/private and numeric aliases preserve the same contract.

HelloNet exposed named unions being indexed as aliases and consequently rejected in an ordinary App_Queue. Added nominal union identity for code resolution; unions remain inadmissible raw wire fields.

The wire fixture pinned old network fingerprints containing raw type spellings. Kept the unchanged ABI/layout fingerprint and exact vector assertions, regenerated base/wide network values, and migrated the assertion, runner and real Session mismatch test together. Current base is 0xbb30630045379ec0; wide is 0xb1c8ea52cdf83fb5.

The legacy shared editor runner swallowed import failures and accepted shutdown resource errors after a success marker. Converted its replacement SceneTree driver to a normal EditorPlugin, checked import/runtime exits and resource errors, and delayed the success marker until cleanup. The strict run passes without hiding errors.

Plain procedure aliases inherit the original private procedure visibility. A rodata procedure-variable attempt is not a valid constant initializer on the pinned compiler and does not support unspecialized generic procedures. Used the independently compiled public `proc {private_proc}` group form instead.

The leaf default tick has no owner callback after extraction, exposing a preexisting invalid generated `_, _ := ...` declaration for discarded results. It now uses assignment when every result is discarded. Owner binding emission also explicitly requests its required intrinsics import.

A private composed procedure in another helper package cannot be bridged from the entity package. Added bridge-only package output in the actual module-local declaring package, then routed both the leaf default thunk and owner binding through that public group. Shared/SDK directories are not written by consumer generation.

Multiple owners could assign different numeric wire IDs to one source symbol, overwriting its identity in metadata. Enforced one stable ID per resolved source across owners; identical declarations may reuse the same ID. Conflicting policies/IDs remain errors.

Field-edge type checks compared only base spellings. They now compare resolved declaration identity, so a genuine alias such as Score=i32 works while an unrelated same-named type cannot pass by spelling.

Generated message routes used package-global Typed_Route storage despite needing per-instance user context. Replaced the generated global with Session-local route registration and an exact-size typed decoder; two game instances now deliver only to their own handlers. The low-level caller-owned Typed_Route API remains available.
The initial schema fixture used app tag9, outside the Session table range0..7. Corrected the fixture to supported free tags4/5 and added a generated compile-time MAX_APP_TAGS assertion.

Codec/blend tags lost their defining scope when a generic field type was rebased. Added a separate tag context and declaration-resolved value references. Module-local private codec getters are contextless so generated descriptor globals can initialize safely; procedure bridges expose private blends.

Old generator tests required global Typed_Route storage and raw tag identifiers. Updated them to require instance-bound routes and resolved numeric tags, retaining typed send wrappers, schema validation and mutation coverage.

Canonical messages no longer serialize tag-name spelling, and redundant root-only profile/message type-spelling walks were removed. Migrated fixed ABI/network test fingerprints together while preserving all exact byte/offset assertions and incompatible-join checks. Current base ABI=0x948638687f891ca8, network=0xe3f298604ea6f896; wide network=0xb961f027c4dd84fb.

The repgen gate still expected direct command callbacks, a hard-coded mask cast, refusal of relative-import composition and the old sample diagnostic. Updated these assertions to bound dispatch, type_of masks, actual replicated imported-field offsets plus compilation, and resolved input identity. Split duplicate-ID, unknown-entity and hook-shape fixtures so an early unresolved symbol does not suppress later binding checks; duplicate IDs now use distinct resolved entity types. The full gate passes.

The event fixture initially used the removed owner,interp spelling; corrected it to owner, which interpolates automatically. Handler-context resolution, both runtime event tables, strict payload bounds, wrong-kind/stale references and manual sim references then pass.

Imported nongeneric backup containers emitted bare private Key/Payload names into the owner package. Keep their declaration context for stable version labels, and infer actual map/dynamic element types from the owner field in generated code. This preserves private types without public bridges. Native cross-read of original saved bytes survives alias, directory and root moves; WASM compilation passes.

Read-only review found a module-wide event-route collision scan using a package-local procedure map. Restricted it to the owning package and added both a legal same-name helper procedure and an illegal owner-package collision.
The first browser fixture placed an added state field before owner, then used a contextful init procedure. Corrected the fixture to the established first-owner and contextless-init contracts.

The browser runtime exposed a real platform defect: knet.subset_view forced the unavailable freestanding heap. A debug WASM stack identified the allocation. The Web host now installs persistent engine storage before authored init procedures and destroys cached views only at final quiescent shutdown. Native keeps the heap default. Focused allocator lifecycle and native Kit net/sim/session suites pass; the ordinary optimized browser export now passes with no console errors.

tasks.title: Support multiple scene variants per Kit entity type
tasks.acceptance: Separate gameplay schema identity from stable scene/variant identity; provide declarative resolver and spawn API without duplicated script structs. Migrate owned protocol/fixtures directly if needed.
tasks.progress: Complete: named scene variants share one gameplay kind, descriptor, callback/census family and typed spawn API. Default scene declarations/calls remain unchanged. Variants survive live spawn, catch-up, resync, recording, save/resume and prediction; incompatible identities and invalid scene roots are refused without publishing partial entities.
implementation_scope: Keep the existing one-scene declaration and spawn calls as the default variant with no new user configuration.
Add stable declarative scene variants without duplicating gameplay structs or replicated schema.
Carry variant selection through authority/client factories, join/interest snapshots, host backup/resume and predicted-spawn reconciliation.
Generate discoverable typed spawn selection and census behavior; migrate owned protocol fixtures directly, test native peers and document the authoring workflow.
changes: Added variant=Name scene tags and generated typed enums with Default=0 and stable FNV32 IDs. Group scene fields by resolved gameplay type before generating helpers; reject missing/duplicate defaults, colliding names/IDs, conflicting gameplay IDs and type policy declarations on variants.

Entity_Kind now holds an explicit scene-choice table, while gameplay callbacks, descriptors and census remain one per type. Added scene metadata to the canonical/structured schema; field order, field renames, source moves and import aliases do not affect variant identity.

Added Scene_Variant to factory callbacks, Session/Boot ledgers and spawn/resync events, with query helpers. The common spawn tuple carries the variant through network catch-up, interest, snapshots, save/resume and recordings. Known-ID resync verifies type and variant before applying fields.

Prediction matches owner/type/variant and returns original spawn identity for command replay. A changed unmatched prediction is canceled and replaced through normal cleanup; authoritative identities cannot be replaced. Bad scene roots are destroyed before entering the tree or census, including with assertions disabled.

Migrated all seven owned custom factory callbacks plus Boot; Session protocol revision is15 and save format is5. Added recording format1 with mandatory protocol and schema checks before packet replay, rejecting old headerless captures without compatibility fallbacks.
HelloSim now uses a default square and Diamond scene with the same Player script. Updated authoring, Session and save documentation; registered kitvariants separately from the fixed core selection.
review_notes: Independent read-only Kit review recommended grouped scene tables, named stable identities, and coverage of every shared tuple path; it confirmed separate Session variant state was a small appropriate change.

Review identified legitimate variant changes during rejection settlement, wrong-root cleanup with assertions disabled, and replay bypassing JOIN compatibility. All three were implemented and given behavioral regression coverage.
test_diagnosis: New native fixtures initially used private packet constants/Tracked types and an Odin redeclaration. Fixtures now capture actual sent packet tags, create predictions through public APIs, and use distinct local names; no implementation checks were weakened.

The invalid-scene fixture omitted Godot’s required include_internal argument to node_get_child_count; corrected the fixture. Both authority and prediction now reject its wrong-script scene with assertions disabled, unchanged published state and no orphan nodes.

The live reject-chain fixture initially issued before lane anchoring and later queried after normal host shutdown cleared the world. It now waits for anchoring and captures successful correction while connected; the actual trace records two executions, different provisional IDs, old_alive=false and a Default replacement after the rejected Equip.

The final thirteen-gate run passed twelve gates; authorsurface found removed-attribute diagnostics inside archived source receipts under docs/replay/results. Corrected only the active-source scan boundary, preserving historical evidence and all prior current-code checks. The targeted rerun passes, as does the additional Kit acid/custom-factory journey.
validation: Latest results are PASS for scriptgen, kitentities, kitvariants, authorsurface, wireabi, kitnet, kitsim, kitsession, kitstress, kitloot, kitarena, kitsave, repgen and kitacid; docs-check also passes.

Codegen runs native tests and freestanding WASM checks. Scene IDs/schema fingerprints stay equal under field reorder/rename, package move and alias changes; a variant-name change changes the contract. One entity kind and one gameplay schema represent both scenes.

Real HelloSim host/guest runs instantiate both authored scenes. Engine probes verify reverse-order predicted matching, provisional aliases, authoritative reuse, cancellation and actual rejected-command settlement replacing the unmatched variant. Standard scene lifecycle also passes.

Session tests verify live/world spawn, late join, interest resync, recording reconstruction, host recovery, identity mismatch refusal, unknown-variant skip and cleanup. The save saga restores the selected scene and preserves it for a reconnecting client.

Recording tests reject wrong magic/format/protocol/schema, truncated headers and old headerless captures before WELCOME, including FINGERPRINT_NONE. Native release-mode probes prove rekeyed identity refusal and wrong-scene cleanup without relying on assertions.

tasks.title: Make Replay authoring tools reusable across games
tasks.acceptance: Replace Scrapyard-specific dock assumptions with capability/action declarations and reusable worker support. Provide a small editor starter with one definition, entity, preview and validation.
tasks.progress: Complete: the dock follows declared actions/inputs, shared workers use remembered tools and structured reports, and Scrapyard callers use the common request contract. The packaged Replay starter includes PickupDef, an authored entity, an isolated preview and validation, sharing one checked extraction and copying rules into World before Session admission.
review_notes: Independent read-only Replay review recommends actions as capabilities, without a second set of enable flags. Start with open_scene, run_scene and project-worker actions; resource/file/text/choice input declarations own their labels, defaults and filters.

The shared worker should parse and validate requests, use the remembered toolchain/build helpers, run bounded headless validation scenes, require structured results and successful exits, preserve logs and cancellation, and keep artifact publication in project handlers.

Snapshot action/input values when clicked, including queued actions waiting for import/status. Only poll status when declared. Render generic details/output navigation instead of Scrapyard casts/health/checkpoint fields.

Extend the existing Replay coin starter with one PickupDef Resource, an authored coin entity, isolated preview and shared typed extraction used by validation and gameplay; copy values into World before Session opens.

Migrate Scrapyard manifest/worker plus workbench and generated scenario CLI callers together. Retain unsaved-input regression coverage and verify a second unrelated tiny project and the installed starter.
test_diagnosis: Queued input values were preserved; the first new assertion compared a Godot-parsed JSON float with an integer inside dictionary equality. Corrected the expected JSON representation, retaining checks for value80 rather than selected index0 and equality with the saved request.

Scrapyard exposed a real SavedData owner bug: inherited StyleBoxTexture resources had both their UI source scene and main.tscn as candidates, but only the source scene serialized them. The plan now proves containment and clears edits only after every proven owner is saved. Genuine stale/orphan/failed-write cases remain refused; added instance and shared-only Resource-edit coverage.

The intentional write-failure fixture left a .tscn replaced by a directory across awaited frames, allowing filesystem import to emit an unrelated dependency error. It now waits for prior scanning and restores the valid file immediately after the synchronous failed save; exact expected save diagnostics and non-publication checks remain.

A generated scenario invocation exposed an obsolete catalog importer using game.CONTENT instead of content.SEMANTIC. Migrated that caller and the authoring validator, and added useful diagnostics to formerly silent tool exits.

Installed-addon verification found SKIP_CORE returned before installing the editor dock. Moved the installation into shared project setup before that return; the fresh package now passes editor, native, peer and browser journeys.

Independent review found failed background status reports could leave Content: current visible. Failures now show issues/logs and a failed status, and recovery replaces that failure. An explicit GDScript boolean type fixed its parse error; the final failure/recovery editor test passes.
changes: Added manifest version1 with open_scene, run_scene and project-worker actions, resource/file/text/choice inputs and optional declared status polling. The dock contains no Scrapyard controls or result-field assumptions; queued actions capture their inputs at click time and expose generic issues, details, outputs and logs.

Added the shared worker/request API, default scene validation, remembered compiler lookup, bounded process ownership and report validation. CLI --action uses declared defaults; --request accepts explicit inputs. Removed the old project-specific CLI and migrated workbench, generated scenario scripts and CI callers.

Fixed SavedData candidate-owner handling: only exact serialization owners are scheduled and used to clear edited flags. Inherited scene resources no longer create false parent-owner failures; all proven owners must save successfully, while orphan/stale/imported/failed-write cases still refuse publication.

Added one PickupDef Resource, one authored pickup scene, standalone F6 preview, validation scene and manifest to the starter. Gameplay, preview and validation share checked typed extraction; gameplay admits a value copy and hashes the authored rules for compatibility.

Moved optional authoring installation before SKIP_CORE returns, so packaged prebuilt-core projects receive their dock. Package snapshots now include authored .tres files and template manifests. Updated framework, starter and Scrapyard documentation.

Migrated the stale Scrapyard catalog semantic caller and improved silent scenario-tool failures. Failed background status checks now show issues/logs rather than retaining a current label, and successful recovery clears the failure.
validation: Five generic contract tests pass, including malformed manifests/requests, actual choice values, no handler load for describe/refused requests, and refusal of missing/malformed reports or failed/erroring validation processes.

An unrelated Orbit project passes actual-editor checks with different actions/resources, no project worker, no undeclared status polling, clickable validation errors, preview without a worker and unsaved tracking. Its worker resolves the saved Odin selection with a minimal GUI PATH.

The complete real-editor save suite passes external/embedded/shared Resources, inherited scene owners, stale objects, closed/released owners, script buffers, failed writes, orphan drafts, transient nodes, edits during jobs, queued input snapshots, cancellation, and failed-status recovery.

The full Scrapyard workflow passes native previews, dock invalid/recovery/bake checks, ability and actor drafts, duplicate refusal, invocation of the generated draft scenario, correction/takeover/network commands, cancellation/non-overwrite checks, 108 Scrapyard model tests, four Stormcaller model tests and native/WASM corpus equality.

A freshly built installed addon passes starter editor invalid/clickable/recovery/preview checks and default worker validation without checkout-relative dependencies. Runtime checks prove invalid preview edits preserve the last valid display, a running World keeps its copied reach, and a new run applies the edited reach to gameplay.
That packaged starter also passes solo pickup/effects, host/client/observer gameplay, native mixer checks, WASM checking and actual browser export execution. docs-check passes.
supported_limits: Authoring process tools remain native macOS/Linux with Python; gameplay native/browser exports are separate. Native editor/runtime acceptance was run on macOS.

Documented scope lifetime, latest-only correction semantics, independent consumers, complete-physics limits and explicit display-time/retirement policy. Fixed build-wait process ancestry detection and allowed isolated-project overrides for migration/menu peer runners.
validation: All 11 setup tests and 184 network tests pass. New coverage includes nil/closed/invalid ownership, Solo/Host/Server/client/observer roles, explicit epoch discovery, two independent correction readers, detached copies, stale/zero refusal, same-generation catch-up and epoch recovery.
A focused rerun after formatting passes, and the public package checks successfully. The real Scrapyard build and freestanding WASM check pass.

Actual actor, feedback and audio checks plus host/client/observer gameplay at120ms latency pass. Planned and host-crash recovery both preserve state and clear old-epoch effects. The separate menu peer flow passes, retaining connection-based choice rebasing.
